newsitem.title: FRANCE: French fin min has no comment on Monde lira report.
newsitem.headline: French fin min has no comment on Monde lira report.

text.p: The French finance ministry declined to comment on a report in French daily Le Monde that France and several other European countries were annoyed with Italian moves to keep the lira from strengthening too much.
"There is no comment," the finance ministry spokeswoman's office said.

Le Monde reported on Tuesday that displeasure in Paris and Bonn over lira sales by the Bank of Italy could delay a lira re-entry into the European Exchange Rate Mechanism (ERM), which Italian Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi has said would happen before the end of November.
The paper said that for the past several weeks the Bank of Italy has been "massively" intervening, through investment funds, to sell the lira whenever it reaches 1,005 per mark.

"We have bought significant quantities of the lira without making the level move," Le Monde quoted an unnamed U.S. fund manager saying. "There is little doubt that an invisible hand is intervening to sell the Italian currency."
Italy and France have been split on the right level for a lira re-entry to the ERM.
"This attitude is not proper," Le Monde quoted a French official saying.

Le Monde said French and German officials have set 950 lira mark as a desired re-entry level, but that the Italian government has been trying to prevent the lira rejoining at what it considers too strong a pivot level.
Italian Finance Minister Vincenzo Visco said on November 6 that 1,000 to 1,050 per mark is the likely range.
